title: Panel collapsed hides its own header, leaving nothing to restore it
foundBy: agents building two consumer apps against 0.2.0, relayed by the repository owner

evidence.verified: `npx vitest run --project browser src/components/Panel.collapse.test.tsx`: 3 tests pass. Collapsed with the default `collapseTo`, the root measures 0px wide and the toggle's left edge sits at or past the root's right edge, where `overflow: hidden` clips it. With `collapseTo="header"` the root keeps its 240px, the title renders, the toggle has a non-zero width and `aria-expanded="false"`, and clicking it calls `onCollapse` once. An expanded panel measures the same width in both modes. Making every mode fold away fails the second test with `expected 0 to be greater than 0`. `collapseTo` reaches `dist/components/Panel.d.ts`, and `npm run ci` exits 0 at 104/104.

details:
Panel's `collapsed` prop sets `width: 0`, `overflow: hidden` and `border-style: none`, all with `!important`. That is the right behaviour for a side panel collapsing to an edge.

In a vertical stack it hides the title bar and any toggle along with the body, so nothing remains on screen to click to restore it. `PanelProps` exposes `width` and no direction, so a consumer cannot ask for the other axis.

Every app that wants a vertical disclosure therefore rebuilds one by hand: a chevron button in the `actions` slot, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` wiring, and CSS to hide the body. That is accessibility plumbing being reimplemented per app, which is what a kit exists to prevent.

The proposal is a disclosure variant, either `collapsible` with a `direction` of `horizontal` or `vertical`, or a dedicated component, keeping the header visible and shipping the toggle and the ARIA wiring.

Worked around in the consuming apps by building that disclosure by hand.

notes.text: Confirmed: the collapsed class cs-component-panel-5 sets width 0, overflow hidden and border-style none, at src/styles/components/panel.css lines 24, 57 and 79. PanelProps at src/components/Panel.tsx:5-14 has no direction and no height.

The repository owner adopted the stopping rule this branch had proposed and never had confirmed: fix the defects a consumer would hit, record everything else, and decide the rest at 0.3.0. This record is one of the six that wait, because each adds or changes a public prop, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks that the design be settled before the code is written.

They are one conversation rather than six, and this is the order they unlock in: CUI-014 first, because whether navigation is a supported use decides CUI-011; then CUI-012, because the `storageKey` convention decides CUI-010; then CUI-009 and CUI-011 together, which are both about sizing to content; and CUI-013 last, which stands alone. The Tooltip and MarkdownMinimap changes that already landed belong in the same conversation.

Nothing here is urgent: every consumer that wanted a vertical disclosure has already built one by hand, so the cost is duplication rather than a broken screen.

Closed with a `collapseTo` prop taking `"edge"` or `"header"`, defaulting to `"edge"`, so no existing panel changes. The owner chose it over a `direction` prop, which names an axis rather than what survives, and over a separate component, which would have duplicated Panel's header, actions slot and ARIA.

This record was larger than the code turned out to be. Panel already rendered the toggle with `aria-expanded` and an "Expand {title} panel" label whenever `onCollapse` was given, so most of the accessibility plumbing the record described was there. What was missing was only the collapse that leaves the header behind.

`aria-controls` was considered and left out. The body is not rendered while collapsed, so it would point at an element that does not exist, and keeping the body mounted in one mode and not the other would be a worse trap than the missing attribute. `aria-expanded` is what the disclosure pattern requires, and `components/Panel.md` says why the other is absent.

No pattern demo collapses a Panel, so nothing downstream moved. The second Explorer card that CUI-011 mentions is still that record's work.
